Balanced but cautious: The FOMC emphasizes strong labor markets and low unemployment, but also notes inflation running below 2 percent and “soft” business fixed investment. In New Keynesian monetary policy frameworks (Clarida, Galí, and Gertler) and Taylor-rule style analyses, this combination justifies holding the policy rate while leaning dovish via forward guidance—especially as market-based inflation compensation has declined and the Fed aims to keep expectations anchored. The weakness in capex aligns with investment literature showing sensitivity to interest rates and financing conditions and amplification through credit markets, with elevated policy uncertainty (Baker, Bloom, and Davis) dampening spending. Bullard’s dissent for a 25 bp cut is consistent with risk-management arguments when inflation is below target. Net tone: mildly positive on current conditions, more cautious on the outlook.
